name: Soncoz
_terms_not_concluded: No terms page found on soncoz.com, so no prohibition could be checked - NOT the same as finding none. Measured 2026-11-25: the only legal page in the navigation is the privacy policy, six likely paths all 404, and the sitemap's support/policies_service.html is an UNFINISHED TEMPLATE whose body is the site-builder's Chinese placeholder, 「请输入要描述的内容进行内容的补充」. The privacy policy was read in full - « Applicable to: soncoz.com and all subdomains » - and covers personal data only. The warranty page was read too, in case a reuse clause hid there; its one reservation is « S ONCOZ(R) reserves the rights to interpret the above warranty . » robots.txt returns 404 with the body « File not found ». Footer: « Copyright (c) 2026 SONCOZ Technology. All rights reserved. » Product pages, specifications, FAQ and the shop are all on the one host, so no shop-scope split arises; the manual archives are served from the site-builder's CDN, which serves no robots.txt either (HTTP 400 on both file hosts).
_the_only_maker_in_this_base_that_number: The SGD1's rear-panel list gives « 3. AES input: 24-bit / 192kHz DSD64 », « 7. Optical input: 24-bit / 192kHz DSD64 » and « 8. Coaxial input: 24-bit / 192kHz DSD64 » as three separate numbered items with their own figures. Musetec, Topping, Shanling, Audio-gd and Aune all give those three sockets ONE combined row. The figures are identical here, which is why it counts: the maker said it socket by socket rather than leaving a reader to assume.
_only_TWO_Soncoz_products_convert_digita: The maker's own navigation groups the range as AMPS (SGP3, SGP1, QXA1), DACS (SGD1, QXD1), PRE-AMP (SGL7, SGA1) and ACCESSORIES (LP1). Only the SGD1 and the QXD1 are converters, and the maker says so of the one that looks like a candidate: « A29: The SGP1 is an analog amplifier with analog input and analog output. » LA-QXD1 and QXD1 are one product - the manual is titled LA-QXD1 and the website's operating text still says « Short press the "Mute" button LA-QXD1 will mute output » - so there is one record, not two.
_no_converter_part_number_anywhere_in_th: « SABRE32 Reference DAC » names a family and not a part, on both models, and neither manual names a converter at all. So `family` is ess_sabre on that phrase and `chip` carries no number. What the maker DOES publish, in its FAQ: « I/V Circuit: OPA1612 * 2; LPF Circuit: RT6863 * 2 », the crystal frequencies « 24 MHz; 45.1584 MHz; 49.152 MHz; 100 MHz », and « It doesn't use a separate receiver chip. The SPDIF signal is processed by the receiver circuit and goes directly into the DAC. »
_the_FAQ_is_a_SPECIFICATION_SOURCE_and_n: Four of the QXD1's most useful facts are on the maker's FAQ page and on no specification table: that DoP is refused and why, that there is no separate S/PDIF receiver chip, that the clock is asynchronous, and which op-amps sit in the I/V and low-pass stages. A harvesting lesson worth keeping: a maker's FAQ can be the only place a MECHANISM is stated, and this was the first harvest in this base to read one.
_a_page_that_serves_no_readable_HTML: The SGD1's product page is built with a JavaScript site builder and returns 50 kB containing only the title to a plain fetch. Its content was recovered from the page's own embedded JSON and the ambiguous parts verified by rendering the page in a browser. A fourth shape of unreadable page, after images, rasterised PDFs and PDFs with no text layer - and the only one so far where the text was there all along, in the payload.
